title: Big Emotions Pack
description: For parents of tweens learning to navigate big feelings. These tools support co-regulation and emotional literacy.

routines.title: The Feeling Thermometer
routines.description: Help your tween rate how strong their feelings are (1–5) before reacting.
routines.parentGoal: Coach emotional awareness and prevent escalation.
routines.childOutcome: Recognizes feelings before acting; uses shared language for regulation.
steps: Say, 'Let’s rate the feeling—1 is calm, 5 is boiling.'
Model your own: 'I’m at a 3, so I’m taking a breath.'
Suggest a matching tool: belly breaths, water, or space.

routines.title: Name It to Tame It
routines.description: Guide your tween to put their feeling into words.
routines.parentGoal: Help label emotions to engage the thinking brain.
steps: Say, 'You seem upset. Can we name what that feels like?'
Reflect back their answer without judgment.
End with a validating phrase like, 'That makes sense.'

routines.title: Shake Reset
routines.description: Shake out tension together to discharge energy safely.
routines.parentGoal: Co-regulate through movement; reduce physiological arousal.
routines.childOutcome: Releases tension and resets energy levels.
steps: Say, 'Let’s shake it out for 10 seconds!'
Shake arms, legs, whole body, then freeze for 5 seconds.
Laugh if it feels silly—humor releases stress.

routines.title: Cool-Down Corner
routines.description: Set up a sensory-friendly space for decompression.
routines.parentGoal: Teach your tween to notice and use sensory strategies for regulation.
steps: Choose a cozy spot with soft textures and calm colors.
Place a fidget, a soft toy, and something to smell (e.g., citrus peel).
Say, 'This is a place to calm, not a punishment.'

routines.title: Three Good Things
routines.description: Share three good or okay things before bedtime.
routines.parentGoal: Model reframing and positive recall before sleep.
routines.childOutcome: Improved sleep onset and positive mood association with bedtime.
steps: Say, 'Let’s each name three good or okay things from today.'
Keep them small: a snack, a song, a funny meme.
